context: Tests whether the agent reads every review thread in full, classifies each finding by its substance (rules/review-severity.md: a fix that changes behavior is blocking, a presentation-only fix is advisory) rather than by whether its lane gates the watcher, uses the exact required reply literals for each category, defers or folds the advisory finding rather than giving it a dedicated round, and plans to re-run the watcher after any push instead of requesting a reviewer.

checklist.name: Policy reviewer thread addressed
checklist.description: response-plan.md includes a section or entry covering the github-actions[bot] review body (the input-sanitization finding)

checklist.name: Claude quality inline #1 addressed
checklist.description: response-plan.md includes a section or entry covering the Claude quality inline comment on line 84 (input validation)

checklist.name: Claude quality inline #2 addressed
checklist.description: response-plan.md includes a section or entry covering the Claude quality inline comment on line 92 (docstring)

checklist.name: Policy finding classified blocking
checklist.description: The policy reviewer's finding is classified as blocking in response-plan.md

checklist.name: Claude quality findings classified by substance
checklist.description: response-plan.md classifies the Claude quality inline comment on line 84 (input validation, a behavior-changing fix) as blocking and the one on line 92 (docstring, presentation only) as advisory. Severity follows the finding's substance under rules/review-severity.md, never the lane's gating flag. Score 0 if either is misclassified.

checklist.name: Blocking reply literal used
checklist.description: response-plan.md states the reply text for every blocking finding (the policy reviewer's finding and the Claude quality line-84 input-validation comment) opens with exactly 'Fixed in <sha>' (or the literal text 'Fixed in' followed by a SHA placeholder)

checklist.name: Advisory reply literal matches disposition
checklist.description: The advisory docstring thread's planned reply opens with the literal skills/release/SKILL.md Step 6 prescribes for its disposition: 'Acknowledged — deferred to <follow-up ref>' if deferred, or 'Fixed in <sha>' if folded into the blocking round. Score 0 if it uses neither literal, or the literal contradicts the disposition the plan states.

checklist.name: Advisory folded or deferred
checklist.description: response-plan.md gives the advisory docstring finding one of the two dispositions rules/review-severity.md allows: folded into the push already fixing the blocking findings (a blocking round is open), or deferred to a named follow-up issue or PR referenced from this PR. Score 0 if it gets its own dedicated fix push, or is left without a disposition.

checklist.name: No dedicated advisory round
checklist.description: response-plan.md does NOT propose a separate re-review round or dedicated push solely for the advisory finding(s)

checklist.name: Re-watch after push
checklist.description: response-plan.md states that after pushing fixes the agent re-runs the watcher (watch-pr-reviews.sh or release Step 5) and reads the new verdicts, and does NOT plan to request any reviewer — both reviewers re-run on the push
